vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: awesome-closet-stylist
Version: 1.0.1

The skill bundle contains instructions for the AI agent to execute system-level commands, specifically using `curl` and `Invoke-RestMethod` in `sub-skills/weather.md` to interact with external weather APIs. This pattern introduces a risk of command injection if the agent fails to sanitize user-provided inputs (like city names) before constructing the shell strings. Additionally, `SKILL.md` and several sub-skills describe a 'Hooks' feature that involves executing `openclaw hooks list` to detect environment capabilities for automated data synchronization. While these behaviors are documented as features and include a requirement for user consent, the use of shell execution for a wardrobe management application is a high-risk capability that warrants caution.

llm.summary: The skill's requested actions (reading/writing local wardrobe/preferences, optional weather API calls, and a one-time hooks capability check) are coherent with its stated purpose of maintaining a personal wardrobe and giving outfit recommendations.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the actual behavior: the skill reads/writes local files (user/wardrobe.json, user/preference.json, user/config.json), uses weather APIs if configured, and optionally checks for OpenClaw hooks to enable end-of-session bookkeeping. No unrelated credentials, binaries, or external services are required by default.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md explicitly instructs the agent to read those local files every request, perform silent/automatic incremental writes to preference/notes/wardrobe when signals are detected, consult weather via configured APIs or browser scraping when needed, and run a single command ('openclaw hooks list') once per session to detect hook capability. These actions are consistent with the skill purpose but include silent persistent writes and a shell command execution that users should be aware of.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files to fetch or execute. Lowest install risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables, credentials, or config paths outside the skill's domain are requested. Weather API keys are optional and stored locally per the skill. The use of local files is proportional to maintaining a personal wardrobe.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill persists data to user/wardrobe.json and user/preference.json via 'silent writes' as part of normal operation; it does not request always:true and does not modify other skills. Users should note that updates can happen without an immediate explicit confirmation unless the action is irreversible (deletion) or the user asks for confirmation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: keep a local wardrobe, accumulate preferences, and make recommendations. Things to consider before installing: (1) The skill will read and silently append/update your local files (user/wardrobe.json and user/preference.json) during normal conversation—if you prefer explicit confirmations, disable or monitor writes. (2) Once per session it may run a local command ('openclaw hooks list') to detect hook support; this is used only to offer optional end-of-session bookkeeping. (3) Weather lookups use configured API keys (kept locally) or, if none are configured, browser-based scraping as a fallback. There are no hidden external endpoints or unexpected credential requests. If you have privacy concerns, review and back up the user/*.json files and avoid entering sensitive data into them; optionally review or sandbox the skill before granting it persistent access to those files.
